newsitem.title: USA: Compaq settles packaging flap with states.
newsitem.headline: Compaq settles packaging flap with states.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp. has agreed to stop providing dealers with factory materials that could be used to repackage old computers and sell them as new, the Texas Attorney General said.

Following a probe into computer industry sales practices, a consortium of 22 state attorneys general alleged that some independent computer dealers were deceiving customers by repackaging and selling as new computers that had been returned or repaired.
"Under the (settlement), Compaq will no longer provide dealers with factory marked boxes and sealing tape," Texas Attorney General Dan Morales said Wednesday in a statement announcing the settlement.

The country's biggest personal computer maker said factory packaging was routinely provided to retailers to replace cartons that were scuffed or dented during shipment, and dealers had been told not to repackage used computers for resale.
In the settlement, filed in a Dallas court, Compaq admitted no wrongdoing but agreed to pay $132,000 to the states to cover attorneys fees and investigative costs.

The Compaq settlement follows a Sept. 5 agreement by Packard Bell Corp., which paid $1.5 million to the states to settle complaints it sold as new computers that contained parts from previously sold computers and monitors.
Packard Bell said recycling components was a common practice in the industry, and agreed to provide retailers with materials to inform consumers of the practice.
